goal: Every read of a store's or the platform's rows filters with owned(): `store_id = $1` for a store and `store_id is null` for the platform, so the store indexes serve it; the cookie scan's due check is served by two indexes and a failing site backs off.
why: Postgres cannot answer `store_id is not distinct from $1` from an index, so the hottest reads scan every store's rows: about 1.2 billion rows read in 78 days on pages, cookie_scans and terms, through 122 uses in 40 files. After: at most 3 commented column-to-column lines, and commerce.cookie_scans' sequential scans grow by fewer than 1,000 a day (about 14,000 a day today).

depends_on.why: the plan asks for two days of production readings on record before this step is deployed, so its 'before' exists

commits.title: owned(): one way to filter a store's rows or the platform's

changes.how: `import "server-only"; import { sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";` and `export const owned = (storeId: string | null, column: SQL = sql`store_id`): SQL => (storeId ? sql`${column} = ${storeId}::uuid` : sql`${column} is null`);` with a doc comment: the one way to filter a store's rows (an equality the store indexes serve) or Kaizena Flow's own (store_id is null); the branch is in code because `store_id = null` matches nothing; `is not distinct from` is not answered from a btree index.

changes.how: In the cookie_scans table's index list (about line 9665) add two indexes on the expression the unique index below them already uses: `index("cookie_scans_site_created_idx").on(sql`coalesce(${t.storeId}, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid)`, t.createdAt.desc())` and `index("cookie_scans_site_done_idx").on(sql`coalesce(${t.storeId}, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid)`, t.finishedAt.desc()).where(sql`${t.status} = 'done'`)`. Then run `pnpm db:generate` (it writes the migration and prunes snapshots) and `pnpm db:check`. Open the generated SQL: it must hold exactly two `CREATE INDEX` statements on commerce.cookie_scans and nothing else. cookie_scans is not one of the hot tables, so a plain create index inside the migration's transaction is right.

In claimScan()'s `last` CTE write the two sub-selects so the new indexes serve them: `where coalesce(c.store_id, ${NO_STORE}::uuid) = coalesce(sites.store_id, ${NO_STORE}::uuid) and c.status = 'done'` for done_at, and the same without the status for tried_at. Add a third column `failures`: `(select count(*)::int from commerce.cookie_scans c where coalesce(c.store_id, ${NO_STORE}::uuid) = coalesce(sites.store_id, ${NO_STORE}::uuid) and c.status = 'failed' and c.created_at > coalesce(<the done_at sub-select>, '-infinity'))`. Replace the retry condition by: `(tried_at is null or tried_at < now() - (case when failures < 3 then ${RETRY_AFTER}::interval else interval '1 day' end))`. Change the order to `order by tried_at nulls first, done_at nulls first` (the site tried longest ago goes first, so a failing site cannot hold the head). The `on conflict` target, the two updates above and the queued claim stay as they are. The file's other uses of `is not distinct from` (4 in all): apply the rule below. In this file replace every `<col> is not distinct from ${<x>}::uuid` where <col> is `store_id` or an aliased `<a>.store_id` and <x> is a JavaScript value (string | null) by `${owned(<x>)}` for a bare `store_id`, or `${owned(<x>, sql`<a>.store_id`)}` for an aliased column (import owned from './owned'). Keep everything else on the line. Where BOTH sides are columns (`a.store_id is not distinct from b.store_id`) and the owner is also available as a JavaScript value in that function, filter each side with owned() on that value instead; where no such value exists, leave the wording and add on the line above it the comment `-- Column to column: both sides may be null (the platform's rows); no parameter to branch on.` Do not touch `is not distinct from` on any column other than store_id, a unique key, or an `on conflict` target. After the edit run this file's own int tests (rg -l '<file name without extension>' src --glob '*.int.test.ts'): they must pass unchanged.

2 uses. In siteFindings() (line 46) write `where coalesce(store_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid) = coalesce(${storeId}::uuid, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid) and status = 'done' order by finished_at desc limit 1`, the form the new partial index serves. In readNotes() (line 55) use `${owned(storeId)}`.

Add two cases beside the pick's existing ones: (1) back-off: a site with three failed scans and no done one is not picked again after 2 hours (move the rows' created_at back with an update), and is picked after 25 hours; a site with one failed scan is picked after 61 minutes; (2) a failing site does not go before a healthy one that is due: site A failed 2 hours ago (one failure), site B's last done scan is 8 days old and was tried 8 days ago: the next claim is B. The existing cases (order of the pick, the hour's retry, one scan per site at a time) must pass unchanged; if the existing order case fails because of the new order by, stop.

Add a small case in the file's style (it applies every migration to PGlite): the two new index names exist on commerce.cookie_scans (`select indexname from pg_indexes where schemaname = 'commerce' and tablename = 'cookie_scans'`).
